To find the characteristic polynomial of a matrix, we need to compute the determinant of the matrix $\mathbf{A} - \lambda \mathbf{I}$, where $\mathbf{I}$ is the identity matrix of the same size as $\mathbf{A}$.

The given matrix is:
$\mathbf{A} = \left(\begin{array}{ccc}
-4 & -13 & 10 \\
-9 & 10 & 4 \\
12 & -5 & -14
\end{array}\right)$

The characteristic polynomial is:
$\det(\mathbf{A} - \lambda \mathbf{I}) = \det\left(\begin{array}{ccc}
-4 - \lambda & -13 & 10 \\
-9 & 10 - \lambda & 4 \\
12 & -5 & -14 - \lambda
\end{array}\right)$

Expanding the determinant, we get:
$\boxed{\lambda^3 + 5\lambda^2 + 21\lambda + 80}$
